title: Learning Rate & Hyperparameters — Choose the Step Size
key_insight: The learning rate controls how far weights move on each update. Too high can make loss bounce or explode; too low can make learning crawl.
body:
## Choose the Step Size

A downhill walker takes giant steps and jumps across the valley. Tiny steps are safe but may never reach the bottom in time.

The learning rate controls how far weights move on each update. Too high can make loss bounce or explode; too low can make learning crawl.

Start from a known reasonable value and watch the loss. Change one setting at a time when building intuition.
common_mistakes: The learning rate is the model’s final accuracy.
Hyperparameters are always discovered perfectly without experiments.
Warmup begins with the largest possible update.
mini_exercise: Sketch the situation in “Choose the Step Size” as three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Good architecture can fail when its training settings make steps unstable, slow, or poorly timed.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “Choose the Step Size” situation, explain Learning Rate & Hyperparameters without assuming the listener knows deep learning.
